title: The mountain of herbs
hookLine: can't tell which herb, so he brings the whole mountain; sankat mochan and seva
last: KARMA: THE FIRE YOU LIGHT COMES HOME.

cards: Night on the battlefield, later in the story, in the war for Lanka. Rama's brother Lakshmana lies struck down by a terrible weapon, barely breathing.
The camp's healer says there's one hope: certain herbs that grow on a mountain in the Himalayas, far to the north. Bring them before sunrise, and he lives.
It's a vast distance, and only one of them could cover it that fast. Hanuman goes. He crosses the land in the dark, finds the mountain, lands, and stops.
There are plants everywhere, glowing in the night. He doesn't know which ones are the herbs. And the sun will not wait.

teach.b: So he picks up the whole mountain. He tears off the peak, balances it on one hand, and flies it back to the battlefield. The healer finds the herbs, and Lakshmana lives.

That image, Hanuman in the sky with a mountain on his palm, turns up on calendars, temple walls and truck doors. The race against sunrise comes from later tellings. Today's word is a name people call him by.
Sankat mochan. Sankat means trouble, a crisis, a tight spot. Mochan means release, setting free.
The one who frees you from trouble. In Varanasi there's a great temple by that name, and people who are frightened, sick, broke or grieving go and stand before him. Look at his choice.
He didn't know exactly what was needed, and he didn't wait until he did. He brought everything.
That's seva, your fifteenth word, at full size: service that doesn't do the minimum.
Now look back at the week. A baby who reached for the sun and came home with every god's gift. A strength forgotten, never lost.
A meeting that began a life of bhakti. A leap made for Rama's work. A story sung softly from a tree.
A fire that came home to the one who lit it.
And a whole mountain, because one leaf might have been the wrong one. Tomorrow, the Ramayana begins, from the very start.

how: Many Hindus call on Hanuman as Sankat Mochan in times of trouble, visiting his temples, including the Sankat Mochan temple in Varanasi, and reciting the Hanuman Chalisa.

games.q: you're Hanuman on a mountain at night. you need one herb before sunrise, and you can't tell which it is. what do you do?
o: search leaf by leaf and hope.
fly back and ask the healer to describe it again.
lift the whole mountain and carry it back.
games.why: he brings the entire peak. the healer finds the herbs, and Lakshmana lives.

practice: A seva review: look back over the last week, at where you served someone, with a favor, a meal, time or attention, and where you did the minimum when you could have brought more. No guilt; this isn't a scoreboard.
Then hold one person in trouble right now in mind. If you pray, say Hanuman's name for them, the way people call on Sankat Mochan. Then ask what bringing the whole mountain would look like for them.

wordCard.voice: Sankat mochan. The one who frees from trouble: Hanuman, who flew a mountain through the night so a friend would live.

orig.note: Hindi, from Sanskrit: the one who frees (mochana) from trouble (sankata).

carryVoice: Your line: seva: bring the whole mountain. Service at full size. Day thirty-five, and Hanuman's week is done.
